answer: Each agent posts a small time-locked deposit before it can act; the bond is refunded with a little nectar-like yield only after an honest epoch. Fake identities must each freeze their own capital for the full lockup, so a thousand sybils cost a thousand idle deposits, and any misbehavior forfeits the stake. Reputation grows like a trellis across epochs: honest agents earn back at near-zero cost, while an attacker pays per identity per epoch, making patience and honesty the cheapest strategy and sybil spam a plume of wasted capital.
